claims: NASA's Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch on Wednesday, April 1, 2026.
NASA's Artemis II mission has a targeted liftoff time of 6:24 p.m. EDT (22:24 UTC).
NASA's Artemis II mission will launch from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B in Florida.
NASA's Artemis II mission is a 10-day crewed test flight around the Moon.
NASA's Artemis II mission will carry four astronauts aboard the SLS rocket and Orion capsule.
The initial launch window for NASA's Artemis II mission opens at 6:24 p.m. EDT on April 1, 2026.
The initial launch window for NASA's Artemis II mission lasts for two hours.
Backup launch opportunities exist for NASA's Artemis II mission if the launch is scrubbed.
Backup launch opportunities for NASA's Artemis II mission have a potential window lasting until April 6, 2026.
Live coverage of NASA's Artemis II mission is available on NASA's YouTube channel.
Live coverage of NASA's Artemis II mission is available on NASA+.
The crew of NASA's Artemis II mission consists of Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, and CSA (Canadian Space Agency) Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen.
NASA's Artemis II mission is the first crewed flight of the Artemis program.
NASA's Artemis II mission aims to test critical life-support systems to prepare for future moon landings.
